description: Change a few lines of an existing class, routine or include file without resending the whole document. Read the exact lines first with a ranged `iris_doc_get` (startLine/endLine): both tools use the same 1-based line numbers. Each edit is an `insert` (afterLine, text, expected; afterLine 0 inserts before line 1), a `delete` (startLine, endLine, expected) or a `replace` (startLine, endLine, text, expected), addressed in the numbering of that read. `expected` is the current text of the lines the edit addresses (for an insert, of line afterLine, or line 1 when afterLine is 0); an edit whose expected text does not match is refused, so an edit never overwrites a line whose text differs from what you expected. `text` and `expected` are plain text: one leading BOM and one trailing line break are ignored, CRLF and LF both separate lines, and an empty text is one empty line (use delete to remove lines). Make `expected` distinctive when a line such as `}` is not unique. All edits apply or none: they are checked together, applied bottom-up against the numbering of the read, and saved in one version-checked write; overlapping edits are rejected. `current` of a STALE_CONTENT mismatch can be passed back as `expected` unchanged, and an `expected` built from a ranged read ends every line, the last included, with a line break. A STALE_CONTENT refusal lists the current text of every mismatched edit, and a DOCUMENT_CONFLICT refusal means the document changed after it was read; nothing is stored in either case, so read the lines again and retry (a conflict is never retried here). For a class, an edit that would drop a Storage definition is refused with STORAGE_DROPPED: keep the Storage lines, or use action `regenerateStorage` to let IRIS regenerate the storage. Returns the result of a fresh read, never the whole document: `unifiedDiff` (3 context lines), an excerpt of each edit (the lines it produced and 3 context lines on each side), `totalLines` and the new version `ts`. IRIS reformats class source when it saves (it adds blank lines between members, for example), so the result can differ from what was sent. The tool does not compile: run `iris_doc_compile` next. Governance: `apply` is a write that is enabled by default. It is disabled when `iris_doc_put` is explicitly disabled (unless `iris_doc_edit:apply` is set explicitly) and under the read-only preset. `regenerateStorage` runs the same edits without the Storage guard and is disabled by default. Human confirmation: when the MCP client supports form elicitation, `regenerateStorage` also asks the person in a confirmation dialog, after every check above and right before the document is saved; only an accept with Confirm ticked proceeds, and a decline or a dismissal returns CONFIRMATION_DECLINED with nothing changed (do not repeat the call unless the person asks). A client without elicitation is not asked, and the call works as described above.

action.description: apply: make the edits, refusing any that would drop a Storage definition of a class (enabled by default). regenerateStorage: the same edits without the Storage guard, so IRIS generates new storage at the next compile (disabled by default).

edits.description: The edits, in any order. All are checked and applied together, or none is.

afterLine.description: Insert only: the text goes after this line, 1-based (0 puts it before line 1). Line numbers are those of `iris_doc_get` for the same document.

endLine.description: Delete and replace: the last line addressed, 1-based and inclusive (not before startLine).

expected.description: The current text of the lines this edit addresses (for an insert, of line afterLine, or of line 1 when afterLine is 0), parsed like text. If it does not match the document now, nothing is changed. Make it distinctive when a line such as `}` is not unique.

op.description: The operation. insert: add text after line afterLine. delete: remove lines startLine to endLine. replace: replace lines startLine to endLine with text.

startLine.description: Delete and replace: the first line addressed, 1-based and inclusive.

text.description: Insert and replace: the new text. One leading byte-order mark and one trailing line break are ignored, and CRLF and LF both separate lines. An empty text is one empty line; to remove lines use delete.

server.description: Named server profile to target for this call (from `IRIS_PROFILES`). Omit to use the default server.

name: iris_doc_edit
title: Edit Document Lines
